precepts.text: There is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty: we usually read this as an individual, but think about it as the nation. Yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate, and lifted up his head from misery; so that many that saw it marvelled at him. The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up, that this low esteemed people now rules the earth.
precepts.point: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. And he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: when you repent and come to this truth, everybody around you starts hating you. And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
There is a difference between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead. “we are in desolate places as dead men,” but Sirach shows what the nation needs: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” We usually read it as an individual, but think about it on a bigger scale. You might say this is Joe or Bob. No, this is us.

Slow, needing help, lacking ability, full of poverty: that is our people. “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,” and lifted up his head from misery, so that many that saw it marvelled at him.

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It will be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth. We lack the ability now; it is the Lord's eye that sets us up from our low estate.

precepts.text: An officer connected it to losing patience in the trial: in the day of prosperity there is a forgetfulness of affliction, and in the day of affliction there is no more remembrance of prosperity. When things go well you forget what the low estate was like; take heed lest you fall. And when the heat gets turned up, you forget the last end, the increase the Lord is going to give you, and the things he has in store. If you would just purge your spirit, you would be able to receive all the things the Lord has promised; but you quit because you forgot what the goal was, you forgot the mission, so you want to abandon ship. Be patient in your lowest state and do not forget the prosperity to come; that strengthens your faith.
precepts.point: They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God. That is how we get saved: as the Most High refines us and burns the iniquity out of us, as we overcome these trials. There is no other way: the fire on one side, the deep water on the other, and the only way through is the straight line. There are no shortcuts for our people; you have to take the long route, because the Most High has to prove you to see if you are worthy of a kingdom.

note.label: Forged by Fire

precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. In that fire some want to quit, stop relying on the brotherhood and abandon ship. Sirach shows why: “In the day of prosperity there is a forgetfulness of affliction: and in the day of affliction there is no more remembrance of prosperity.”

In the day when things are going well, you forget what it was like to be in your lowest state, and you have to take heed lest you fall. And in the day of affliction, when the fire comes up and the heat gets turned up, you forget the prosperity: the last end, the increase the Lord is going to give you, the things he has in store.

The trying of your faith worketh patience, and Sirach 2 says, woe unto them that have lost patience. If you would just purge your spirit, you would be able to receive all the things the Lord has promised for the future. But you quit because you forgot what the goal was; you forgot the mission, so you want to abandon ship.

When you are going through that adversity, be patient in your lowest state and don't forget the prosperity to come. That is what strengthens your faith through the refining, until the Lord says, “It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

precepts.text: You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. You look foolish when you do this without understanding what's going on. Your opinion, if it lacks understanding, if it lacks the pertinent information that needs to be used in order to explain what's going on, but you feel necessary to give that opinion, something is wrong with you. You've been put in many situations that have shown you: yeah, you jumped the gun. But yet and still, you feel your opinion matters. It don't. Understand first, and then rebuke.
precepts.point: That's the type of people you don't know for exhorting anybody. You only know them for bringing problems about everything they see, but they lack exhortation in any form.

note.label: Jude 1:16

precepts.why:
We were warned: “in the last days perilous times shall come”, and among the men of those days are “false accusers.” Sirach gives the law against it: “Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.”

You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. How many people run their mouth without understanding, without knowing? How many gossip without the full understanding of what is going on, yet have so many opinions and thoughts on how this should be, on what so-and-so is doing and shouldn’t be doing? You look foolish when you do this without understanding what is going on.

If your opinion lacks understanding, if it lacks the pertinent information needed to explain what is going on, but you still feel it necessary to give it, something is wrong with you. You have been put in many situations that showed you that you jumped the gun, that you didn’t know what was going on. Yet and still you feel your opinion matters. It doesn’t. Understand first, and then rebuke.

That goes with the pride Paul names. The prideful spirit won’t allow you to take any correction or accept what is being said; it has you thinking it is everybody but you. And it goes with the “despisers of those that are good”: people who hate that you are doing what you are supposed to do, that you are above them in rank and active in the body. Every time you turn around they have a suggestion nobody asked for, and they don’t say it to you; they tell everybody underneath you, so all your peers know how they feel. You never know them for exhorting anybody, only for bringing problems about everything they see.

The law says “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people.” The talebearer with the tea, who somehow knows before leadership knows, is the fuel that keeps reputations scarred and people at odds. And when you tell a story as if you know what is going on, without the whole story, and it is not true, that is a lie: “he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.” That is why you must examine the truth before you blame.

precepts.text: There is another that is slow, wanting ability and full of poverty; yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good and set him up from his low estate and lifted up his head from misery, so that many marvelled.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
For the brother who says he has a reading impediment, or that his eyes hurt: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” This is a brother who is mentally slow, lacking ability, and poor.

“yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate”. The Lord lifted his head from misery, so that many who saw it marveled. It is the same as James's brother of low degree who rejoices that he is exalted.

So it is not impossible, but give the Lord something to work with. Show him that you believe and have faith, and he can do wonders. If you want to lose weight, get in the gym, eat smaller portions, walk around the block once, then twice, and let the Lord do the rest. Instead of five pieces of chicken, eat one; you won't die. In the same way, put on Bible audio if reading is hard. Do your part and the eye of the Lord will look upon you for good.

precepts.text: Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men; a brother starting from the bottom at a job does not matter. Commend not a man for his beauty, neither abhor a man for his outward appearance. How many sisters were deceived by a good-looking man before the truth? Every woman wants a man, and a woman who says she does not need one goes against nature: her hormones release when she is under her husband, which is why she falls asleep ten minutes into the movie she asked to watch. She is bone of his bone, made in his image, which is why little girls look like their daddy; the body is the portal but the seed comes from the man. Sisters, release the feminism.
precepts.point: There is a friend who being turned to enmity and strife will discover thy reproach, and some friend is a companion at the table and will not continue in the day of thy affliction. Sirach 11:29, bring not every man into thine house, for the deceitful man hath many trains, sits with these; Sirach 6 through 15 connect, from proving a friend to not letting just anyone stroll into your house, with chapter 12 adding trust not thine enemy, for as iron rusteth so is his wickedness. You cannot know someone in three months or even a year: a person of twenty-seven has twenty-six years you know nothing of, family history, mental illness, diabetes, disease.

note.label: Our Forefathers Built This; We as Sons Must Preserve This!

precepts.why:
“If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him.” In the forties they understood it takes time to know someone’s true intentions: you could court her, but on the front porch in front of everybody, no dates, no secret meetings. “For some man is a friend for his own occasion”: some just want sex, men and women, and we have them among us. When you look across the room, you are not wondering if she can help with your resume. You are thinking about the curves, the lips, the perfume. When you learn the truth and the fear of the Lord, you realize it is more than how she looks, and the same for the sisters.

Sirach says: “Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men.” Whatever the brother’s finances, even if he is just starting at the bottom of a job, none of that matters. Wisdom lifts up his head and sets him among great men.

“Commend not a man for his beauty; neither abhor a man for his outward appearance.” Sisters, how many of you were deceived by a good-looking man before you came into this truth? Don’t raise your hand. And don’t let social media fool you: every woman wants a man. A woman who says she doesn’t need one is going against nature. Her body releases hormones when she is under her husband; that is why she falls asleep ten minutes into the movie she asked you to watch. All her fear goes out the window, because she is safe.

She is bone of his bone, flesh of his flesh, made in the man’s image, and she is his glory. That is why little girls look like their daddy: her body is the portal that brings us into this life, but the seed comes from the man. Sisters in the truth who walk around like they don’t need their husband, release the feminism.

So don’t pass over a good brother because of his outward appearance. A sister told a captain she couldn’t see herself with a good brother; did you see yourself forty-something and not married? Prove a man by his wisdom and intentions, not his looks.

precepts.text: Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not.
precepts.point: A captain charged after an attack on him and his wife was cleared when video showed he defended himself. Many had already believed the one-sided account.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” That is why so many brothers get caught up in suits: striving in things that do not concern them, things they know nothing about. You just hear something and you are running your mouth.

To sit in judgment with sinners is sitting in counsel with brothers that are not right, brothers who were put out of the school, like Judah Mack and Titus.

Read on: “My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent.” This is for those who keep running their mouths talking about us. You meddle in matters that do not concern you, and you are not going to be innocent. That is why legal measures are being taken: to teach men to control their mouths, and to make sure that when you say something, it is true.

So the privy slanderer of Psalms 101 is the man who strives in what does not concern him and sits with sinners, and God will cut him off.

precepts.text: Do not be hasty to credit somebody for their beauty or their outward appearance.
precepts.point: Do not be hasty to credit somebody based on their looks. Of course you want somebody you are attracted to, but commending a person for beauty alone gets a lot of people in trouble.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

precepts.why:
“Commend not a man for his beauty; neither abhor a man for his outward appearance.” Do not be hasty to credit somebody based on their looks.

Jacob loved Rachel because she “was beautiful and well favoured”, while Leah “was tender eyed”. Of course you want somebody you are attracted to, but commending a person for beauty alone gets a lot of people in trouble. That is the caution to carry alongside Jacob's seven years: beauty is what he saw, and it is not enough by itself to commend anyone.

precepts.text: Micah brought every man into his house and lost everything in it; the deceitful man has many trains, many tricks and approaches.
precepts.point: The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren, because the deceitful man has many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

precepts.why:
“Bring not every man into thine house: for the deceitful man hath many trains.” Micah brought every man into his house and lost everything in it. The first time the five spies lodged with him they saw his expensive looking gods and got covetous; now, passing back through with six hundred men appointed with weapons of war, they tell their brethren, “Do ye know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image, and a molten image? now therefore consider what ye have to do.” On the way to the lick they spotted another lick.

Many trains means many tricks and approaches to finesse you out of the goods in your house. The Bible addresses everything: do not bring just anybody into your house, even brethren.

precepts.text: For your newer brothers and sisters, Ecclesiasticus is the book also called Sirach: prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, all come of the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” Ecclesiasticus, the book also called Sirach, says the same: “Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord.”

All of it comes of the Lord, the poverty and the riches, the bringing low and the lifting up.

precepts.text: How is that possible? It is the Lord: he brings low, and he lifts up one that was never thought of. Like David: when Samuel looked at the older brother he thought, he has to be the one, he looks like a king; but the Lord chose the one sitting down upon the ground whom nobody thought of to be the king.
precepts.point: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.” Out of the dust means out of confusion: he brings the poor out of confusion, “and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory.”

“Many kings have sat down upon the ground; and one that was never thought of hath worn the crown.” How is that possible? It is the Lord: he brings low, and he lifts up one that was never thought of.

Like David. When Samuel looked at the older brother he thought, he has to be the one, he looks like a king. But the Lord chose the one sitting down upon the ground, whom nobody thought of, to be the king. All of it is his, “for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.”

precepts.text: In the day of prosperity there is forgetfulness of affliction, and in the day of affliction no more remembrance of prosperity; people forget to save and prepare when things go well, and forget past prosperity when things go wrong.
precepts.point: In my prosperity I said I shall never be moved: the key point of making the Most High your refuge and salvation is staying on the right path regardless, whether prosperity or affliction comes.

note.label: Psalm 30: Joy Cometh in the Morning

precepts.why:
“And in my prosperity I said, I shall never be moved.” Ecclesiasticus shows what prosperity does to the mind: “In the day of prosperity there is a forgetfulness of affliction: and in the day of affliction there is no more remembrance of prosperity.”

People forget to save and prepare when things go well, and forget past prosperity when things go wrong. The key point of making the Most High your refuge and salvation is staying on the right path regardless, whether prosperity or affliction comes.

precepts.text: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches all come of the Lord; you prospered one time and now you are in your season of adversity.
precepts.point: Whoso is wise and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord. If you have wisdom you will observe these things.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord.” All of it comes of him.

That is the psalm: “Again, they are minished and brought low through oppression, affliction, and sorrow”, meaning we go back into slavery, and yet he sets the poor on high from affliction. You prospered one time, and now you are in your season of adversity. Whoso is wise and will observe these things will understand the lovingkindness of the Lord in both.

precepts.text: Hear the matter fully before answering; that is wisdom and discipline.
precepts.point: A wounded spirit no man can bear.

note.label: Proverbs 18: The Power of the Tongue and Righteous Judgment

precepts.why:
“He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.” Ecclesiasticus gives the same: “Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.”

Hear the matter fully before answering; blame not before examining the truth, and interrupt not men in the midst of their talk. Understand first, and then rebuke. That is wisdom and discipline.

precepts.text: Do not strive in a matter that does not concern you.
precepts.point: As a madman who casts firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man that deceives his neighbor and says, "Am I not in sport?"

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.” Grab a dog by the ears and you are going to get bitten; that is what meddling in strife that is not yours gets you.

Ecclesiasticus gives the same warning: “Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” Do not strive in a matter that does not concern you.

A young lady who tried to break up a high-school fight was grabbed by police, slammed face-first, and left with brain damage. She took the dog by the ears in strife that was not hers. The Bible is a true book.

points: There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: Whereas he saith, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

So you got this man, he works hard, he becomes rich. He got paid real well. He got a nice house, nice cars, top notch. He is living well. His wife is living well. He said, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods. And I know this man do not give a damn about these brothers. He do not give a damn about the sisters. He said, I am going to continue to eat. Look at me, I got all this wealth. And yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him. In other words, this man has no idea what is about to happen tomorrow, because this man says he is always going to be good. He is always good in the neighbourhood. No, he is not always going to be good.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced; and the honourable delivered into other men's hands.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke. Answer not before thou hast heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talk. That is why we did not move right away, because we needed some time to process what was going on, to let it play itself out.

Sometimes you do not interrupt men in the midst of their talk because they are putting their foot in their mouth. Let your yeas be yea and your nays be nay. They think they are going to explain themselves out of the situation. Did you take money? Did you steal? No. But what do you consider stealing? I experienced that before, and it was not here, it was someplace else. I said, hey brother, did you steal? He said, No, I borrowed some money, but I put it back. I said, Did you ask? He said, No, but I put it back. I said, You do not understand that is stealing? If you went to the bank and you took money without asking, and then you came back a week later and put it back, you think you would not get arrested for that? I said, Bro, you are a thief. You took without asking. How do you not understand that?

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Like as a partridge taken and kept in a cage, so is the heart of the proud; and like as a spy, watcheth he for thy fall. He will watch for your demise, your fall.

That is what the Pharisees did with Christ. All the good that Christ was teaching. No, no, he said he is going to overthrow Rome, he is going to destroy the temple. And they are going to lay blame on you.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

points: Receive a stranger into thine house, and he will disturb thee, and turn thee out of thine own. So I know brothers are inviting people over to their house to learn the scriptures. That is fine. But be mindful of that. You do not know all these brothers. You do not know their wife. You do not know their kids. You just know that brother's name is Shabazz or Hakeem or whatever. That is all you know. And you are bringing them over to your house with your wife and children. Be very careful. And for you simple brothers that go into a brother's house and bring in another brother that the brother whose house it is does not know, that is evil and stupid. You have to be wiser than that. You have to wait until you get to know him.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

points: Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: y'all know black people, we love jumping to conclusions. We love that thing. We watch a movie; movie been on for three minutes; we like, yep, he evil, that's the bad guy; yeah, I already know how this going to end. Black people, we got superpowers. Understand first, understand first, and then rebuke.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

points: My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent; and if thou follow after, thou shalt not obtain, neither shalt thou escape by fleeing.

Oh no, you're in it now. You wanted to know what the flavor of the Kool-Aid was; now you're making the Kool-Aid. It's all yours. All because you wanted to be in someone else's business. The scripture says, meddle not.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: A sister in Columbia was shown a good brother, own business booked through March, speaks multiple languages, in the green, good-looking, and said she could not see herself with him. Did you see yourself forty-something and not married? Women stuck in Disney and Love and Hip Hop waiting for Prince Charming miss good husbands, and a father's job is guiding the daughters' minds toward what a good man is.

Before a brother even asks about a sister, we have grilled him: pull up the Chime app, let me see the Wells Fargo and the Chase account. Three hundred dollars and a light bill of three-fifty, and you think I would give my baby to a man who cannot buy her shoes? Fathers do the math on the car note and the bills; that is why the Bible says commend not a man for his beauty, because every brother is not Boris Kodjoe or Idris Elba.

My grandmother, married forty-seven years, would say that's Shemar Moore in front of my grandfather as he left for work with his back bad. That is not a small thing; it is disrespect, and it is why women fall into lust and adultery or leave a husband who just does not do it for her anymore.

A quiet light-skinned sister came into the body with a big buff brother who never asked questions; she would not be with him until he came in and married her, and his weak nature bugged out. Years later a diligent officer asked about her, and six months into proving she called my wife crying that he was not her type physically. Did the type you were attracted to not have sex with you and leave? They married, and at the men's conference in 2024 she confessed adultery with her boss, who looked exactly like the first brother. She never got over the lust from the world, the Lord blocked the children, and the brother divorced her; Jeremiah 3, she had to go. Commend a man for his beauty and you end up with an ungodly man, or take anyone because you are in your thirties and think you should be married by now.

note.label: Our Forefathers Built This; We as Sons Must Preserve This!

points: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord. You will always find them together; in prosperity you never know a friend, in adversity you learn he never was one. So do not fear these things when they happen, and stop asking the Lord for blessings and jobs while doing nothing to earn them.
